guides.title: Make Text Bigger
guides.description: Make the letters on your screen larger so they are easier to read.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
steps.image_alt: Settings app icon on the Home screen
steps.genz_note: Small text? No stress. We fix it together, no cap.

steps.text: Tap Display & Brightness.
steps.genz_note: One tap at a time. You ate that.

steps.text: Tap Text Size.
steps.genz_note: Almost there. Let me cook.

steps.text: Drag the slider to select the font size you want.
steps.genz_note: Big letters! let's gooo!

tips: Need it even bigger? Go to Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size, tap Larger Text, then drag the slider.
If the text gets too big to tap buttons comfortably, come back to these settings and make it smaller.

verification.applies_to: General Android (used for Xiaomi and OPPO). Menu names can differ by brand. Google notes some steps work only on Android 13 and up.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
steps.genz_note: Small text? No stress. We fix it together, no cap.

steps.text: Search for Font size and select it.
steps.image_alt: Search box at the top of Settings
steps.genz_note: One tap at a time. You ate that.

steps.text: Move the slider left or right to choose your font size.
steps.genz_note: Almost there. Let me cook.

tips: Quick way: swipe down from the top of the screen and tap Font Size. This tile is added automatically after you change the font size from Settings.
Font size can go up to 200%.

verification.notes: Microsoft's page does not mention an Apply button. Step 4 is worded 'if you see' for that reason; confirm on your own laptop.

steps.genz_note: Big letters! let's gooo!

tips: This makes only the text bigger. To make images and apps bigger too, open the Display button under Related settings on the Text size page, then choose an option from the Scale list.

guides.title: Take a Screenshot
guides.description: Save a picture of what is on your screen, for example a message or a bill.

verification.applies_to: iPhones with Face ID (no Home button).

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture
steps.genz_note: This one is fun. Let me cook.

steps.text: Press the side button and the volume up button at the same time, then quickly let go.
steps.image_alt: Side button and Volume Up button highlighted

steps.text: On iOS 26 the screenshot appears with quick tools: tap the save button to choose where to save it. On iOS 18 and earlier, a small thumbnail appears in the lower-left corner: tap it to open the screenshot, or swipe it left to dismiss it.

tips: To find your screenshots later: open Photos, go to Collections, tap Media Types, then tap Screenshots.

verification.applies_to: General Android (used for OPPO). Button layouts differ by brand.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture
steps.genz_note: This one is fun. Let me cook.

steps.text: Press the Power and Volume down buttons at the same time.
steps.image_alt: Power and Volume Down buttons highlighted

steps.text: To find it: open the Photos app, tap Collections at the bottom, then On this device, then Screenshots.

tips: If that does not work, hold the Power button for a few seconds, then tap Screenshot.
On older Android versions without Photos, open the Gallery app and look in the Screenshots folder.

verification.notes: Microsoft's page does not describe dragging to select an area, so that detail is left out.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to capture.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture
steps.genz_note: This one is fun. Let me cook.

steps.text: Press the Windows logo key + Shift + S together to open the snipping overlay.
steps.image_alt: Windows, Shift and S keys highlighted

steps.text: The screen turns slightly gray. This means you are ready to capture a snip.
steps.image_alt: Dimmed screen ready for a snip

tips: After you capture a snip, it appears in the Snipping Tool window and is saved automatically to your Screenshots folder.
Press the Print Screen key (PrtSc) to copy a picture of your whole screen to the clipboard.

steps.text: To capture the whole screen, press Shift, Command and 3 together.
steps.genz_note: This one is fun. Let me cook.

steps.text: To capture part of the screen, press Shift, Command and 4 together, then drag the crosshair over the area you want.
steps.image_alt: Crosshair selecting part of the screen

steps.text: By default, screenshots save to your desktop. If a thumbnail appears in the corner, click it to edit the screenshot.

tips: Shift, Command and 5 opens the Screenshot app. You can also find it in the Utilities folder of your Applications folder.
Hold Control with the shortcut (for example Control, Shift, Command and 3) to copy the screenshot to the clipboard instead of saving it.
You can change where screenshots are saved in the Screenshot app's Options menu.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture
steps.genz_note: This one is fun. Let me cook.

steps.text: Press and hold the Power (Side) button and the Volume down button at the same time, then let go after a brief moment.
steps.image_alt: Side button and Volume Down button highlighted

steps.text: The screen flashes. To find it: open the Gallery app, tap Albums, then open the Screenshots folder.

tips: Palm swipe: open the Quick panel, tap the gear icon, go to Advanced features, then turn on Palm swipe to capture. After that, swipe the edge of your hand across the screen to capture.
You can also find screenshots in My Files under Images.

verification.applies_to: Xiaomi and Redmi phones. Xiaomi's page does not name specific models, and menus may differ on newer HyperOS.

steps.text: Open the screen you want to save.
steps.image_alt: Any screen you want to capture
steps.genz_note: This one is fun. Let me cook.

steps.text: Swipe down from the status bar at the top of the screen to open Control Center.
steps.image_alt: Swipe down from the status bar

steps.text: Tap Screenshot.

tips: You can also slide three fingers down the screen to capture. To turn this on (or the Volume down + Power buttons), open Settings > Additional settings > Gesture shortcuts > Take a screenshot.

guides.title: Turn On the Flashlight
guides.description: Use your phone's built-in torch in the dark.

steps.text: Swipe down from the upper-right corner of the screen to open Control Center. On an iPhone with a Home button, swipe up from the bottom edge instead.
steps.genz_note: Torch time. let's gooo!

steps.text: Tap the Flashlight button.
To turn it off, tap the Flashlight button again.

tips: On the Lock Screen, press and hold the Flashlight button in the bottom-left corner.
To change the brightness: open Control Center, press and hold the Flashlight button, then drag the slider up or down.
If the button is missing, go to Settings > Control Center and tap Flashlight in the list of available controls.

steps.text: Swipe down from the top-right corner of the screen to open Quick settings.
steps.image_alt: Swipe down to open Quick settings
steps.genz_note: Torch time. let's gooo!

steps.text: Find the Flashlight icon. If you cannot see it, swipe left.
Tap the Flashlight icon to turn the light on or off.

tips: To change the brightness: open Quick settings, press and hold the Flashlight icon, turn the flashlight on with the switch, then drag the slider. The slider stays grayed out until the flashlight is on.

guides.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
guides.description: Join your home Wi-Fi so you can use the internet without using mobile data.

steps.text: Open the Settings app and tap Wi-Fi, then turn on Wi-Fi.
steps.image_alt: Wi-Fi row at the top of Settings
steps.genz_note: First step soon. Lowkey easy.

steps.text: Tap the name of the Wi-Fi network you want to join.
steps.genz_note: You are doing great, no cap.

steps.text: If it asks, enter the network's password.
Look for a blue checkmark beside the network name. This means you are connected.
steps.image_alt: Blue checkmark next to the network

tips: If you do not know the password, ask whoever manages the network.

verification.applies_to: General Android (used for Xiaomi and OPPO). Menu names differ by brand.

steps.text: Open your phone's Settings app.
steps.genz_note: First step soon. Lowkey easy.

steps.text: Tap Network & internet, then tap Internet.
steps.genz_note: You are doing great, no cap.

steps.text: Tap a listed network. Networks that need a password show a lock icon.

tips: Shortcut: swipe down from the top of the screen, tap Internet, and pick a network in the panel that appears.

steps.text: Click the Network, Sound or Battery icons in the taskbar at the bottom-right of the screen to open quick settings.
steps.image_alt: Network, sound and battery icons in the taskbar
steps.genz_note: First step soon. Lowkey easy.

steps.text: In the Wi-Fi quick setting, click Manage Wi-Fi connections (the arrow next to it).
steps.image_alt: Arrow next to the Wi-Fi button
steps.genz_note: You are doing great, no cap.

steps.text: Choose the network you want, then click Connect.
Enter the network password and click Next.

tips: If your network is not listed, click the Refresh network list button in the lower right.

steps.text: Open the Settings app.
steps.genz_note: First step soon. Lowkey easy.

steps.text: Tap Connections.
steps.genz_note: You are doing great, no cap.

steps.text: Tap Wi-Fi. If it is off, tap the switch to turn it on.
Tap the name of the Wi-Fi network you want to connect to.
If it asks, type the password and tap Connect.
When you are connected, the network name appears under Current network with Connected below it.
Click the Network, Sound or Battery icons in the taskbar at the bottom-right of the screen to open quick settings.

guides.title: Block Spam Calls
guides.description: Stop unwanted numbers from calling you again and again.

verification.applies_to: iPhone Phone app. The Info button applies to Classic view.

steps.text: Open the Phone app, tap Recents, then tap the phone number or contact you want to block.
Open the entry's Info button.
steps.image_alt: Info button next to a recent call

steps.text: Scroll down and tap Block Caller.

tips: To see or unblock numbers on iOS 26: Settings > Privacy & Security > Blocked Contacts. Tap Edit, tap the delete control beside the contact, then tap Unblock.

verification.applies_to: Android phones using the Google Phone app. Other phone apps may use different menu names.

steps.text: Open the Phone app, tap More, then tap Call history.
Tap a call from the number you want to block.
Tap Block / report spam.

tips: To unblock: open the Phone app, tap More, then Settings, then Blocked numbers. Next to the number, tap Clear, then Unblock.

guides.title: Update an App
guides.description: Keep apps like WhatsApp up to date with the latest features and security fixes.

verification.applies_to: iPhone apps from the App Store.

steps.text: Open the App Store.
Tap the My Account button or your photo at the top of the screen.
steps.image_alt: Profile photo in the App Store

steps.text: Tap App Updates, then tap Update next to an app, or tap Update All.
steps.image_alt: App Updates list with Update button
steps.genz_note: A little refresh for your apps. Nice!

tips: Apps from the App Store update automatically by default. You can still update one by hand if something is wrong.

steps.text: Open the Play Store app.
Tap your account icon in the top-right corner.
Tap Manage apps & device.
steps.genz_note: You're in the right place. Keep going!

steps.text: Under Updates available, tap See details. Then tap Update next to an app, or tap Update all.

tips: To control automatic updates, go to Settings > Network Preferences > Auto-update apps. You can choose over Wi-Fi or mobile data, limited mobile data, Wi-Fi only, or no auto-update.

guides.title: Volume and Brightness
guides.description: Make your screen easier to see and your phone louder or quieter.

verification.applies_to: iPhone. This guide covers brightness only; volume steps are not included because no Apple page was available to check.

steps.text: Open Control Center: on an iPhone X or later, swipe down from the top-right corner. On an iPhone 8 or earlier, swipe up from the bottom edge.
steps.image_alt: Opening Control Center on an iPhone

steps.text: Drag the brightness bar up or down.
steps.genz_note: Nice and clear — you've got this.

steps.text: Or open Settings, tap Display & Brightness, and drag the slider right or left.

verification.applies_to: General Android. Appearance and menu names can differ by brand and Android version.

steps.text: Press a volume button on the side of your phone.
steps.image_alt: Volume buttons on an Android phone

steps.text: Tap the menu icon on the right of the volume bar.
steps.image_alt: Menu icon on the volume bar
steps.genz_note: Louder and clearer — you've got this.

steps.text: Move the sliders (Media, Call, Ring, Notification and Alarm volume) to the levels you like.
To change brightness, swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings.
Move the brightness slider left to dim the screen or right to brighten it.

tips: On older Android versions, tap the down arrow on the volume bar instead, then choose Media, Ring or Alarm.
You can also change volumes in Settings > Sound.

guides.title: Delete a Photo
guides.description: Delete an unwanted photo and learn how to get it back if you removed it by mistake.

steps.text: Open Photos and select the photo you want to delete.
steps.image_alt: Photo open in the Photos app
steps.genz_note: A little photo cleanup — let's do it carefully.

steps.text: Tap the Trash button, then tap Delete Photo.
If you deleted it by mistake: in Photos, swipe up and tap Recently Deleted in the Utilities section, then tap View Album.
Unlock the album with Face ID or Touch ID. Tap the photo, then tap Recover (or tap Select, choose your photos, tap More, then Recover) and confirm.

tips: Items stay in Recently Deleted for 30 days, then they are removed permanently.
If iCloud Photos is on, deleting a photo on one device removes it from every device signed in with the same Apple Account.

steps.text: Open Google Photos. Touch and hold the photo you want to remove.
steps.genz_note: A little photo cleanup — let's do it carefully.

steps.text: Tap the Trash icon at the bottom.
To get it back: tap Collections, then Trash.
Touch and hold the photo, then tap Restore at the bottom.

tips: Items stay in the trash for 30 days, then they are permanently deleted.
Deleting from Google Photos also deletes the same item from your device, and from other devices that have backup on.

verification.applies_to: Gallery app on Samsung Galaxy phones.

steps.text: Open Gallery, tap Pictures or Albums, and find the photo. Tap it to select it.
steps.genz_note: A little photo cleanup — let's do it carefully.

steps.text: Tap Delete at the bottom of the screen, then tap Move to Trash.
To get it back: open Gallery, tap the menu icon (three lines), then tap Trash.
Touch and hold the photo, then tap Restore at the bottom of the screen.

tips: Deleted items stay in the Trash for 30 days before they are permanently deleted.

guides.title: Find Your Screenshots
guides.description: Find the screenshots you have taken on your phone.

steps.text: Open Photos.
steps.genz_note: Let's find that missing memory.

steps.text: Go to Collections and tap Media Types.
Tap Screenshots.

verification.applies_to: Google Photos on Android. On older Android versions without Photos, use the Gallery app.

steps.text: Open the Photos app.
steps.genz_note: Let's find that missing memory.

steps.text: Tap Collections at the bottom, then tap On this device.
Tap Screenshots.

tips: On older Android versions without Photos, open the Gallery app and look in the Screenshots folder.

verification.applies_to: Gallery app on Samsung Galaxy phones.

steps.text: Open the Gallery app.
steps.genz_note: Let's find that missing memory.

steps.text: Tap Albums.
Open the Screenshots folder.

tips: You can also find screenshots in My Files under Images.
